note: Media entity Lottie adds a core Media source plugin 'lottie_file' (extends core File, restricts the source field to the json extension, exposes metadata w/h/nm/v/fr, adds a lottie_file upload validation constraint) and a field formatter 'file_lottie_player' (extends FileMediaFormatterBase, renders <lottie-player>, only applicable to a field whose name contains field_media_lottie_file, settings: background, background_transparent, hover, mode, speed, count + play_when_visible). There is no settings form (configure=null). Config lives in the media type (media.type.<id> source=lottie_file) and the view display (core.entity_view_display.media.<id>.default formatter file_lottie_player). Medium cases create a namespaced Lottie media type (mel_src / mel_disp) and read back its source/extension and its Lottie player display settings; hard cases build a Lottie media type (mel_build) and turn on hover-to-play on a Lottie player display (mel_task), verified against live config. All fixtures create and tear down their own mel_* media types + source fields.

evals.prompt: I want Drupal's Media system to store and manage Lottie animations using the media_entity_lottie module. Which media source do I choose when creating the media type, and what file extension does its source field accept?
evals.expected_output: Create a media type with media source 'Lottie file' (plugin id lottie_file). Its source field is a file field restricted to the json extension (Lottie animations are .json).

evals.prompt: How does media_entity_lottie render a Lottie animation on the page? Name the field formatter and the HTML element it outputs, and one playback option it exposes.
evals.expected_output: The 'file_lottie_player' (Lottie player) field formatter renders each file as a <lottie-player> web-component element and attaches the lottie-player JS library. Options include background/transparent, hover (play on hover), play when visible, mode (normal/bounce), speed, and count (loop count).

evals.prompt: What does the media_entity_lottie upload validator (the lottie_file constraint) check before accepting an uploaded file?
evals.expected_output: The lottie_file constraint rejects the file if it is empty, is not valid JSON, or does not contain the required Lottie animation keys (fr, ip, op, w, h, ddd). Keys v and nm are optional (a warning is shown if missing).

evals.prompt: This site has a media type named 'MEL Source' (id mel_src). Inspect the live configuration and state which media source plugin it uses and which file extension its source field accepts.
evals.expected_output: The mel_src media type uses the lottie_file source; its source field is a file field limited to the json extension.

evals.prompt: The media type 'MEL Disp' (id mel_disp) has its Lottie player display formatter customized. Inspect the live default view display and report the configured playback speed and whether it plays on hover.
evals.expected_output: In core.entity_view_display.media.mel_disp.default the source field uses the file_lottie_player formatter with speed = 3 and hover = true.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the media_entity_lottie module to create a media type with machine id 'mel_build' that stores Lottie animations (uses the Lottie file source with a json-only source field). Apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create a media type mel_build with source lottie_file, create its source field (a file field, file_extensions json) and set source_configuration.source_field. Verified by loading the media type: source is lottie_file and its source field accepts json.

evals.prompt: The media type 'mel_task' on this site renders Lottie animations with the Lottie player. Configure its default display so the animation plays on mouse hover. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: In core.entity_view_display.media.mel_task.default set the source field's file_lottie_player formatter setting hover = true. Verified against the live view display.
